## What The Business Is

Corning Inc. is a 175-year-old materials-science company built around glass science, ceramic science, optical physics, and precision manufacturing. Its current markets include optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, display, automotive, solar, semiconductors, and life sciences. In Q1 2026, Corning changed its reporting structure: **Optical Communications** and **Automotive** remain standalone; **Glass Innovations** combines former Display and Specialty Materials; **Solar** includes Hemlock polysilicon plus solar wafer/module operations; and remaining activities sit in Life Sciences and Emerging Growth Businesses. ([corning.com](https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/about-us/news-events/news-releases/2026/05/nvidia-and-corning-announce-long-term-partnership-to-strengthen-us-manufacturing-for-ai-infrastructure.html))

## What It Does

Corning makes optical fiber, cable, and connectivity systems for carrier and enterprise networks; display glass for TVs, notebooks, and monitors; Gorilla Glass and advanced optics for mobile devices, semiconductor optics, aerospace/defense and other uses; ceramic substrates and filters for emissions control; life-sciences labware and bioprocessing products; and solar/semiconductor polysilicon, wafers, and modules. Its optical business is increasingly tied to AI data-center scale-out, while its Glass Innovations segment remains exposed to consumer electronics, displays, and semiconductor optics. ([corning.com](https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/about-us/corning-business-segments.html))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Corning’s Q1 2026 results were strong: core sales rose **18% YoY to $4.35 billion**, core EPS rose **30% to $0.70**, core operating margin expanded **220 bps to 20.2%**, and adjusted free cash flow was **$188 million**. Optical Communications was the standout, with sales up **36% YoY to $1.846 billion** and segment net income up **93%**; Solar sales rose **80% YoY to $370 million**. Management said results were led by Optical Communications and Solar, consistent with the transcript excerpt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000198/glw-20260328xex991xq12026.htm))

Corning materially raised its long-range growth framework at its May 6, 2026 investor event. The company said it expects a **$20 billion annualized sales run rate by end-2026**, upgraded its 2028 internal Springboard plan to a **$30 billion annualized run rate**, and extended the plan to a **$40 billion annualized run rate by end-2030**; it also introduced a new Photonics market-access platform targeting a **$10 billion revenue stream by 2030**. ([corning.com](https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/about-us/news-events/news-releases/2026/05/corning-upgrades-and-extends-springboard-plan-outlines-new-phase-of-accelerating-growth.html))

The AI-infrastructure customer pipeline expanded after quarter-end. On May 6, NVIDIA and Corning announced a multiyear commercial and technology partnership under which Corning plans to expand U.S. optical connectivity capacity **10x**, expand U.S. fiber production capacity by **more than 50%**, build three new plants in North Carolina and Texas, and create more than 3,000 jobs. On June 8, Amazon announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with Corning for optical fiber, cable, and connectivity solutions supporting U.S. data-center infrastructure, tied to 1,000 new jobs at Corning’s North Carolina facilities. ([corning.com](https://www.corning.com/worldwide/en/about-us/news-events/news-releases/2026/05/nvidia-and-corning-announce-long-term-partnership-to-strengthen-us-manufacturing-for-ai-infrastructure.html))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Solar execution remains a near-term drag despite strong revenue growth. In the transcript, management said the solar wafer ramp was “running behind” plan; the Q1 release confirmed an extended maintenance shutdown at the solar wafer facility, including transition to permanent power and equipment repairs/upgrades, adding **$30 million** of Q2 expense versus Q1. Solar segment net income was only **$7 million** in Q1 2026, down **74% YoY** and **77% sequentially**, despite the 80% sales increase. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000198/glw-20260328xex991xq12026.htm))

Not all segments are participating equally. In Q1, Glass Innovations sales were up only **1% YoY** and down **5% sequentially**, while Automotive sales fell **1% YoY**. Management also flagged that rising memory costs could significantly affect the 2026 consumer-device market, even while it expects Corning’s premium products to outperform. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000198/glw-20260328xex991xq12026.htm))

The growth plan depends on large capacity expansions, customer-funded/risk-sharing arrangements, government incentives, and sustained AI-infrastructure

- AI optical demand is inflecting: Optical Comms sales +36% YoY, segment net income +93%, with multiyear NVIDIA (10x connectivity capacity, +50% fiber capacity) and Amazon (multibillion-dollar) agreements underwriting the build-out.
- Management raised guidance to a $20B annualized run rate by end-2026 and $30B by 2028 — implying ~20%+ revenue CAGR versus TTM $16.3B — plus a new $10B Photonics platform by 2030.

Customer-funded/risk-shared capex and government incentives cushion the balance sheet during expansion. Sustained hyperscaler visibility could keep the multiple at or above current premium levels, supporting EV well above $180B.

- The stock already prices extraordinary success: EV/FCF is ~110x (FCF/EV yield 0.9%), far below the 3-year average yield of 1.8%. Any AI-capex digestion pause could compress the multiple sharply.

- **EV:** 2,200 × 78 ≈ **$171,600M**.

## Bull Case
Optical Communications is inflecting hard on AI data-center demand, evidenced by 36% YoY segment growth, the NVIDIA 10x capacity partnership, and the Amazon multibillion-dollar deal. Management's $20B run-rate by end-2026 implies TTM revenue climbing well above the current $16.3B. If revenue grows ~20% to ~$19.5B and FCF conversion improves with operating leverage (margins expanding 220bps), forward FCF could reach ~$2,300M. Buyers reward the AI-infrastructure narrative with a premium EV/FCF multiple near ~100x (rich, but consistent with the elevated current valuation and high-growth optical mix), supporting meaningful market-cap upside.

## Bear Case
Solar execution is slipping (wafer ramp behind, $30M extra Q2 expense, segment income down 74% YoY), Glass Innovations is flat, and Automotive is declining. Rising memory costs threaten the consumer-device market. The current EV/FCF yield of ~0.9% is extraordinarily stretched; any AI-capex normalization compresses the multiple. If FCF only reaches ~$1,900M and the multiple contracts toward the 3-year average yield (~1.77% FCF/EV ≈ 56x), EV falls sharply and market cap could decline materially.

## Logic
- TTM FCF = $1,511M; TTM net income = $1,810M; revenue = $16,321M.
